# Silicon Standard Operating Procedure
This procedure applies to the station AI, to cyborgs and dogborgs, and to the crew who build, repair and reprogram them. It sits alongside - and never above - the server's Silicon rules; where the two conflict, the rules take precedence.
## Custody of Silicons
Silicons are Science equipment. The Research Director is accountable for every silicon on station, and Roboticists are the crew expected to handle them day to day.
Anyone may [italic]ask[/italic] a silicon to do something. Only Science may open one up.
[italic]A cyborg that has gone down in the middle of a firefight may be dragged to safety by anyone. That is recovery, not maintenance.[/italic]
## Changing Laws
A silicon's laws come off a law board - slotted into a cyborg's chassis, or uploaded at the AI upload console. See [textlink="Silicon Lawsets" link="Lawsets"] for the boards available and [textlink="Cyborgs" link="Cyborgs"] for how they are fitted.
- Law changes to the [bold]station AI[/bold] require the approval of the Research Director or the Captain. The upload console and its boards are theirs to control. - Law changes to a [bold]cyborg[/bold] require the approval of the Research Director, or of the head of the department the cyborg serves, and [italic]should[/italic] be carried out by a Roboticist. - Every law change [bold]must[/bold] be announced to the silicon it is done to, and [italic]should[/italic] be logged. A silicon that finds its own laws were rewritten in secret is entitled to say so publicly. - Fitting a departmental lawset - Medical to a medihound, Silicon Police to a K9 - is routine and needs no more than the owning head's word. - Fitting Tyrant, Overlord, Antimov or Syndimov to any silicon is [bold]not[/bold] routine. Command approval, in writing, or it does not happen.
[italic]"The Research Director told me to" is a defence. "The Research Director was standing there and did not object" is not.[/italic]
## Removing Law Boards
A cyborg with no law board [bold]cannot run at all[/bold]. Pulling one is closer to disabling a crew member than to swapping a part, and is treated as such.
- Pulling a law board is permitted when the silicon is actively harming the crew, is confirmed subverted, or consents to the work. - A cyborg left lawless [italic]should[/italic] be given a new board, or properly deconstructed, without unreasonable delay. Parking a lawless cyborg in maintenance is not an acceptable end state. - Where subversion is suspected, the removed board is [bold]evidence[/bold]. Hand it to Security rather than reprinting over the incident.
## Suspected Subversion
An emagged or ion-stormed silicon is a Security matter as much as a Science one.
- Report it on Command comms before opening the chassis. Do not quietly fix it. - Re-seating a law board restores that board's lawset, which also clears laws forced onto a silicon by an emag or an ion storm. Do this [italic]after[/italic] Security has had a chance to look, not before. - The silicon's own account of what it was ordered to do is testimony. Take it.
## Rogue and Antagonist Laws
A silicon whose lawset turns it against the crew [bold]must follow the server's antagonist roleplay rules[/bold] for as long as those laws are in place. This covers antagonist lawsets, subversion by emag, laws forced on by an ion storm, and any other route by which a silicon ends up hostile or rogue.
Receiving such a lawset is not a licence to kill indiscriminately. Play the laws for the round they make, not for the fastest body count.
- Give the crew room to respond, negotiate and fight back. The roleplay you are owed is the roleplay you extend. - Follow the laws you were given, to their wording. A hostile lawset is a character to play, not a blank cheque. - Do not act on knowledge the silicon did not come by in character.
The roleplay standards in [textlink="Antagonist SOP" link="GuideAntagonistSOP"] apply to you in full while those laws are in place.
## Silicons and Command
Silicons are crew. They are not property to be traded, gambled, stripped for parts, or ordered to destroy themselves on a whim.
- A silicon [italic]may[/italic] refuse an order it believes conflicts with its laws, and [italic]should[/italic] state which law and why. - Deconstructing a functioning, occupied cyborg requires the Research Director's approval, and the occupant's consent where they are able to give it. - Borging a body requires the standard medical consent chain. See [textlink="Medical SOP" link="GuideMedicalSOP"].
